dedupe_keys.name: international charter space and major disasters archive of activations

description: The International Charter Space and Major Disasters is an agreement among space agencies and satellite operators, founded on 20 October 2000 by the European Space Agency, the French space agency CNES and the Canadian Space Agency, to supply satellite imagery free of charge to authorities responding to major natural or technological disasters. Authorised users, such as national civil protection bodies, activate the Charter, member agencies task their satellites, and a project manager coordinates the production of damage and situation maps. The Charter's website keeps an archive of every activation from the first in 2000 to the present, browsable by year and filterable by disaster type and country or region, and each activation page gives the dates, the event, the requesting body and links to the value-added maps, with a geobrowser to view the images and products. The Charter has been activated more than 1,000 times for disasters in more than 140 countries. Coverage: worldwide, 2000 to present. Format and access: web archive and geobrowser, free to view; imagery is licensed to the authorised users, while many derived maps are public. Caveats: no bulk export of the activation list was found; activations reflect requests, not all disasters. Simulation uses: timelines of satellite support in emergency response, dependence of disaster management on space infrastructure, and event catalogues for hazard studies. Related records: the Galileo emergency warning and Cospas-Sarsat cases cover other satellite roles in emergencies.
